prompt: Create a high-fidelity desktop web app UI mockup for Aftertaste, a Russian personal cultural diary, edge to edge landscape 1440 × 1000, no device, browser frame or surroundings. It is a real B2C screen for browsing saved books, films, series, theatre, music and exhibitions, not a landing page. Adult, luxurious retro character inspired by vinyl record sleeves and the precision of classic film cameras. The user explicitly chose a light gallery combined with a deep cool burgundy header, charcoal ink, restrained silver-grey details and clear near-white surfaces. No olive, khaki, yellow, cartoon illustration, fake distressed paper, giant decorative vinyl, photographic camera hero, dashboard statistics or CRM/table layout. Keep a tiny vinyl circle beside the lowercase wordmark “aftertaste”. Type should evoke Prata for a modest headline and entry names, Onest for interface labels, fully readable Cyrillic. Standard web search, category buttons, date/year filters and one “Добавить запись” action. Real labels: “Сколько по десятибалльной?”, “Все”, “Книги”, “Фильмы”, “Сериалы”, “Спектакли”, “Музыкальные альбомы”, “Выставки и музеи”, “Поиск по названию”, “Год”. Show six demonstration entries under “Сентябрь 2026”: “Нормальные люди” Книга 9/10, “Прошлые жизни” Фильм 8/10, “Вишнёвый сад” Спектакль 9/10, “Медведь” Сериал 8/10, “In Rainbows” Radiohead 9/10, “ГЭС-2” Выставка 8/10. Each card has one sophisticated photographic main image, name, category and wine-coloured score; use plausible cinematic/stage, book and vinyl imagery, not toy category objects. Full review and other photos belong in the detail view. Small footer “Демонстрационные записи”. Composition B — compact collection-led. Keep the same brand world, slim burgundy brand header and light workspace, but make the collection materially denser: three columns of compact horizontal cards, each with a substantial 3:2 photographic thumbnail on its left and title/category/score to its right. Two complete rows should be visible comfortably, with the next month starting below. Use delicate rounded rectangles with quiet tonal separation, no table headers or columns. Controls remain above the cards. This should feel like a beautifully maintained private cultural library with convenient browsing, never administration software.
